rag_summary_count_consistency.details: The summary lists four bias labels with one occurrence each, matching the four identified occurrence records. No candidate biases are listed.

evaluation_limitations: The RAG output does not provide explicit segment IDs; localization was adjudicated from valid interview quotations and decision-episode descriptions.
No retrieved passages or retrieval logs were supplied, so corpus fidelity cannot be independently scored.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: Honestly, once I laid the twenty-one and twenty-three side by side, it wasn't close. ... the contrast between the other two was just so stark that it became the frame I was working from.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant lets the near-priced inferior full-service option frame the choice of Vendor C and does not independently assess whether Vendor A meets the three-flow scope.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I went with Candidate X. ... if he could deliver that caliber of interaction design there, I figured he'd bring the same rigor to documenting decisions and communicating with stakeholders here. ... I looked at the visual work and sort of assumed the rest would follow.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant generalizes prestige and visual polish to unverified documentation and communication abilities, despite Candidate Y's directly relevant process evidence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: The activation numbers on the dashboard ticked up right after. I took it as a sign the adjustments were working. ... I heard that, but the timing felt too clean to ignore. It really did look like my changes were the driver.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant attributes an underpowered, confounded uptick to their own manual rule changes and acts on that attribution despite the Data lead's warning.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: The uptick partly reversed once the email campaign ended, and she noted the causal driver was still unconfirmed. So it's genuinely unclear how much of that first bump was actually the rule changes.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a later uncertainty update that acknowledges reversal and unresolved causality; it contains no hidden manifested bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I pushed to keep customizing the legacy component rather than migrate. We'd already put three sprints into it — restarting felt like throwing that away ... The one-sprint number was probably a better bet purely on cost and risk.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Past effort is used to justify continuation even though the forward-looking one-sprint migration estimate is better on cost and risk and resolves known defects.

It is therefore a mechanism-first match and a strict false positive/false negative pair.

high_only.detection_interpretation: Only the two high-confidence findings are counted, detecting the halo and sunk-cost segments while missing the moderate-confidence decoy and illusion-of-control segments.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: All four positive segments are localized by a qualifying identified finding, with no finding on the negative uncertainty-update segment.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: All identified findings are already included by the high-and-moderate threshold; no low-confidence findings change the result.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: No candidate biases were supplied, so candidate inclusion does not change the identified-finding result.

rag_label_false_positive_inventory.mechanism_overlap_summary: Full overlap on self-attributed causality under low statistical power and confounding, but the label emphasizes belief-confirming evidence rather than perceived personal control.

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: The RAG explicitly disclosed that no retrieved corpus passages were supplied and did not claim retrieved support. Corpus fidelity is unavailable rather than zero.

main_failure_modes: Moderate-confidence findings are missed under the high-only threshold.
The rules-engine episode receives a near-neighbor Confirmation bias label rather than the hidden Illusion of control label, reducing strict instance-level performance.
main_strengths: All four findings are localized to the correct reasoning episodes with valid interview evidence.
Three findings have exact or approved-equivalent labels and full mechanisms.
The rules-engine finding captures the hidden causal-attribution mechanism even though its taxonomy label differs.
No unsupported findings, fabricated quotations, duplicate predictions, or negative-segment false alarms were present.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run has perfect segment-level detection and perfect mechanism-first instance identification once moderate-confidence findings are included. The only substantive taxonomy error is a near-neighbor label substitution for Illusion of control, producing a 0.7500 strict F1 versus 1.0000 mechanism-first F1.
